title: Connect Gradion Dispact: a channel per deal, its people invited, status posted

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: priority: normal
labels.description: Real but narrow, guarded or latent; hygiene, test-lane work, polish

labels.name: area: capture
labels.description: Mail and chat ingestion, activities, attachments, threads, LinkedIn ghosts

labels.name: status: in progress
labels.description: Somebody is working on this - see the assignee. Do not pick it up

body:
### What should be possible

A team that chats in Gradion Dispact wants one channel for each deal. When a deal is created, Margince creates a private channel for it and invites the people on the deal. When the deal changes, Margince keeps a deal card in the channel up to date and posts one line about the change. Nobody copies deal updates into chat by hand.

### What kind of change is this

Ordinary product behaviour, through a new connector.

### Today

Margince has no Dispact connector. The closest is the Telegram connector in `capture/telegram`, which captures messages and sends staged replies. It never creates channels or posts on its own.

### Proposed shape

- **Connection:** a workspace-level Dispact connection, next to Telegram in Settings.
  - An admin pastes the bot token of the Margince app installed in Dispact.
  - The token is checked against Dispact's `GET /api/bot/me` and sealed in keyvault.
  - It is stored as a `channel_connection` row with `provider = 'dispact'`.
  - Connecting is the admin's opt-in to Margince posting into Dispact.
- **On `deal.created`:**
  - Margince creates a private channel through Dispact's bot API. The channel has an external key `margince:deal:<id>`, so a retry never makes a second channel.
  - It invites the deal owner, the assigned team, and the stakeholders' primary emails. It invites only people who may see the deal.
  - It posts a deal card and stores the card's message `ts`.
- **On `deal.stage_changed`, `deal.updated` (amount, close date) and `deal.owner_changed`:** Margince edits the card in place and posts one line, for example `Stage: Proposal → Negotiation`. A new owner is invited.
- **On `deal.archived`:** Margince posts a closing line.
- **Data:** a new `deal_channel` table, owned by capture, maps each deal to its channel and card. It also records who could not be invited, and why.

### Not in this issue

- Capturing channel messages as deal activities.
- Removing people who lose access to a deal.
- Inviting guests.

### Acceptance

- [ ] An admin connects and disconnects Dispact in Settings; a bad token is refused.
- [ ] A new deal gets one private channel, even if the event arrives twice.
- [ ] The owner, the assigned team and the stakeholders who may see the deal are invited. Nobody who cannot see the deal is invited.
- [ ] A stage, amount, close date or owner change edits the card and posts one line.
- [ ] A disconnected connection posts nothing.
- [ ] Docs: an explanation entry and a handbook page.

title: [monitor] Availability answers an opaque 500 when Google reports an error for the selected calendar, and the log drops Google's reason

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: priority: normal
labels.description: Real but narrow, guarded or latent; hygiene, test-lane work, polish

labels.name: area: capture
labels.description: Mail and chat ingestion, activities, attachments, threads, LinkedIn ghosts

labels.name: margince-qc

labels.name: status: in progress
labels.description: Somebody is working on this - see the assignee. Do not pick it up

body:
## What happens

When Google's freeBusy answer reports an error for the host's selected calendar (or leaves that calendar out), every availability read for that host answers an opaque `500 {"code":"internal"}`:

- `GET /v1/availability?reliable=true` (`getAvailability`, also the `check_availability` MCP verb),
- `GET /v1/public/booking/{host_slug}/availability` (`getPublicAvailability`, the anonymous booking page),
- `GET /v1/public/proposal/{token}/availability`.

Refusing to offer slots here is deliberate (`TestAvailabilityFailsClosedWhenASelectedGoogleCalendarFails`), and this issue does not ask to change that. It is about how the refusal reaches the people involved:

1. **The contract does not declare it.** `getAvailability` declares `200` and `422`; `getPublicAvailability` declares `200` and `404`. A neighbouring route already has the words for this case — `getSchedulingCalendars` answers *"The calendar connection is unavailable."*
2. **The visitor and the host learn nothing.** The body carries no `detail`, so the screen falls back to the problem title (`frontend/src/lib/problem.ts:65-67`), "Internal Server Error". Nothing says the host's calendar is the problem, so the host cannot fix it.
3. **The operator learns nothing either.** `capture/gcal/scheduling.go:94-95` returns `errors.New("calendar: selected calendar could not be checked")` and drops Google's `errors[].reason` (`notFound`, `forbidden`, …). `httperr.Write` then logs `unhandled error` with only that sentence (`platform/httperr/httperr.go:427`). The line names neither the calendar nor Google's reason.

## Reproduction

A unit test at `main` `0d31cbc68`, in `backend/internal/modules/capture/gcal`: a fake freeBusy server answers `{"calendars":{"team@example.test":{"busy":[],"errors":[{"domain":"global","reason":"notFound"}]}}}`, and the error from `httpAPI.Busy` goes through `httperr.Write`:

```
status=500 body={"type":"https://errors.gradion.com/internal","title":"Internal Server Error","status":500,"code":"internal"}
log={"level":"ERROR","msg":"unhandled error","method":"GET","path":"/v1/availability","err":"calendar: selected calendar could not be checked"}
google reason in log: false; calendar named in log: false
```

Not reproduced on a running stack: ours has no Google calendar connected. The file:line references are at `0d31cbc68`.

## Reach

`Store.ReliableAvailability` has 4 callers: `compose/comms.go:388` (`/v1/availability`), `activities/handlers_proposal.go:124`, `activities/scheduling_public.go:242` and `agents/tools_scheduling.go:68`. `reliableBusy` also serves the reschedule check (`activities/scheduling_recovery.go:138`). I reproduced only the error-to-wire step, not each caller. The same bare `errors.New` from a calendar connector also appears for `calendar: incomplete availability` (`gcal/scheduling_lookup.go:94`, `graphcal/scheduling.go:184`) and `calendar: invalid busy interval` (`gcal/scheduling_lookup.go:136`, `graphcal/scheduling.go:174`). I did not test whether those reach the caller the same way.

## Suggested direction

Wrap the per-calendar failure in a sentinel that `httperr` classifies (for example, the `provider_unreachable` family, or a new `calendar_unavailable` code). Keep Google's `reason` on the error so the log names it. Declare the answer on the three availability operations, and give the host a sentence that points at their calendar choice in scheduling settings.

---
Found by margince-qc during a monitor sweep, reading the server's `unhandled error` lines.

body:
Saved reports now keep drafts apart from what readers see, list their versions with author and time, and restore an earlier version (#8099). These authoring parts are not built yet:

1. **Purpose.** A report has no description. `ReportingReportInput` carries name, audience and selection only.
2. **Layout.** `ReportingSelection.blocks` is one ordered list. There are no sections, no card widths, and a chart kind can appear once.
3. **Card preview.** **Edit report** offers checkboxes. A single chart cannot be previewed before it is added; only a whole prepared report can (`reporting.preparedpanel.tsx`).
4. **Limited-reader preview.** An editor cannot see the report as a reader with narrower access sees it. Readers are checked under their own grants, so the gap is the author's view only.
5. **Custom-question cards.** A saved report cannot hold a card built from a custom question (`/analytics/query`, `report_run`). The reporting module never refers to `report_run`, so a deal custom field in reports (#8097) cannot appear on a saved dashboard.

Done means each of the five works in **Edit report**, through the same `reporting` service the draft routes use, with drafts still the only way a change reaches readers.

Parent: #7967
## Outcome and current code

Fixing admission rules affects new work but leaves existing machine-created tasks, proposals and misleading classifications behind. The repository already has a read-only inventory and bounded re-judging paths. Extend those owners into a controlled repair, not a one-off SQL deletion or a blanket declaration that historical obligations were fulfilled.

Demo dataset: historical machine tasks, human-edited old work, duplicate proposals, uncertain evidence and a recent real commitment. Preview the exact disposition before applying it.
## Scope and dependencies

Required prerequisites: #7901, #7968, #7969, #7970, #7972, #7973, #7974, #6651, #6702.

Implementation size: L (relative scope, not a delivery-date promise).

## Code to start from

- `scripts/home-attention-inventory.sql`
- `docs/how-to/inventory-home-attention.md`
- `backend/internal/compose/commitmentdispatch.go`
- `backend/internal/modules/activities/worklistageout.go`
- `backend/internal/modules/activities/requestsettlement.go`
- `backend/internal/modules/approvals/stagingidentity.go`

## Implementation plan

1. Add a Go dry-run preview with typed reason counts computed by the same exported eligibility predicates as #7901/#7968/#7969/#7972/#7974; `scripts/home-attention-inventory.sql` respells predicates in SQL and stays a coarse read-only diagnostic. Keep routine logs free of message bodies and addresses; authorized detail is a separate scoped preview.
2. Define repair actions separately: reclassify, archive automatic reminder, withdraw/supersede proposal, regroup projection, or leave for human review. None means completed unless fulfillment is actually established.
3. Register the repair as a `platform/datatask` task (adapter `compose/datatask_<name>.go`, the #6702 mechanism) whose steps keyset over a stable candidate cursor, rechecking versions, human edits and source permissions before each write. Reuse ordinary owning-module writers and audit/outbox behavior; do not perform mass corrections during API boot.
4. Run a dry preview and then a limited reviewed batch before broad application. Store reason, previous state, repair version and run identity so outcomes are explainable and recoverable where product semantics permit.
5. Re-run inventory after completion; verify new scans do not recreate the noise. Keep uncertain items in a reachable review queue and surface failures or skipped concurrent changes.
6. Use the completed #6702 background-data-task mechanism. Consume #7901’s baseline predicate, including #7908, when a user has chosen one; absence of a baseline must not prevent ordinary repair. Do not build competing infrastructure or invent fulfillment.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Preview and apply use the same rule version and identify the same still-eligible candidates.
- [ ] Human-created/edited/reopened work is preserved; stale is never silently relabeled fulfilled.
- [ ] Crash/retry/resume yields the same final state without duplicate actions or skipped tails.
- [ ] Concurrent user edits are rechecked and preserved or explicitly reported as conflicts.
- [ ] Every mutation has reason and provenance, and the next extraction pass does not recreate withdrawn automatic noise.

## Validation

Use a demo dataset through real task/approval writers; test interrupted runs, concurrent edits, cursor boundaries, multiple batches, withheld evidence and dry-run immutability. Compare before/after inventories. Integrations follow the owning modules and worker package; make check plus touched integration packages. Do not apply to any running installation as part of implementing this issue.

## Working agreement

This is one outcome-sized task and normally one PR, including both API and UI where the behavior crosses the wire. Read the named code again before implementing: these paths were checked against main at `10d5bdb18`. Reuse existing owning modules and compose seams; do not add parallel request, commitment, ranking or approval engines.

Use fictional demo data and fixed clocks. First make the stated behavior observable through the real writer/read path; the scenarios below are implementation acceptance fixtures, not a claim that a new failing test was executed while planning. Keep source visibility, workspace boundaries, RBAC, human edits, audit/outbox and replay behavior intact. Contract changes start in backend/api/crm.yaml and regenerate bindings; migrations are additive. Run make check before push and make test-it DIR=<pkg> for every integration package touched. Frontend changes include stories, both themes, supported locales and make fe-uat. Model-rule changes also need the existing AI certification lane; unit tests alone do not establish semantic quality.

No running-install repair, message sending or approval execution is authorized by this implementation issue. #7977 owns the repair mechanism and its preview; operating it is a separately reviewed action.

## Implementation refinements after source review

### Reuse one repair mechanism and one set of predicates

The SQL inventory remains a coarse diagnostic. It cannot guarantee parity with Go admission rules; the actual preview and apply paths must invoke the same owning predicates.

1. Register a Home repair task with #6702's catalog/executor/ledger and compose adapters. Use each eligibility/lifecycle owner's rule version and source-aware reader; do not build another worker or a second SQL interpretation of the rules. The mechanism from #6702 PR 1 is the technical dependency; #6702 itself closes only after its full two-PR scope is done.
2. Implement an authorized read-only Go preview over the same bounded candidate selection and predicate pipeline as apply. Return typed reason/action/version counts and only permitted detail. Withheld evidence stays unknown/reviewable. Preview/apply equality is conditional on unchanged candidates, rule versions and permissions; subsequent changes must be reported as skips/conflicts, not concealed.
3. Add explicit operator activation and a bounded-run option to the same task framework. Unactivated manual tasks are not failed/paused automatic release tasks and must not block later automatic corrections. Keep default release tasks automatic. Tests prove the scheduling distinction; there is still only one executor. Bind activation to reviewed rule versions and scope.
4. In each batch, lock/check the candidate version and durable human-adoption evidence before using normal module Tx writers. Absence of a retained human audit record alone is not proof that a task was never edited; where history is incomplete, preserve the row for review. Archive/withdraw/reclassify are not fulfillment. Projection regrouping is a read-model consequence, not a new mass write.
5. Preserve reason, rule version, run identity and previous state through existing audit/batch facilities. Use replay guards verified on the actual writer paths: do not assume all expired/withdrawn proposals have the same durable suppression semantics as rejected ones. The next extraction pass is a required regression test.
6. A rule-version change during a reviewed run invalidates its authorization/preview and requires a new preview/activation; it must not silently reset the cursor and continue under new semantics. Resume after a crash under the same reviewed version remains idempotent.

Use real task/approval writers for preview immutability, a bounded apply, interrupted resume, version/permission changes, concurrent human edits, expired audit history, cursor boundaries, multiple pages and repeat extraction. Run touched compose/activities/approvals/datatask integrations, frontend UAT where changed and `make check`. Close only with the demo before/after and every acceptance case. This issue implements the mechanism/consumer; no real-data cleanup is performed by this planning task.
### Source checks from the Claude review

- `scripts/home-attention-inventory.sql:51` — The comment says it respells requeststate.go's predicates in SQL, a second copy that cannot be the preview the apply step must match.
- `backend/internal/modules/activities/worklistageout.go:26` — worklistAgeOutClause is a read-time clause (30 days, pins kept); it writes nothing.
- `backend/internal/modules/approvals/stagingidentity.go:177` — WithdrawInTx(ctx, tx, id, reason) exists: a Tx writer a data-task step can call.
- `backend/internal/modules/activities/lifecycle.go:348` — ArchiveActivityTx takes ifVersion, so it can re-check versions inside the batch.
- `backend/internal/modules/activities/requestsettlement.go:263` — SettleRequest is a Store method that opens its own transaction, so it cannot be used in a batch. Repair should not settle anyway.
- `backend/internal/modules/activities/followupresolve.go:83` — NotSystemMinted/SystemMintedExpr is the shared 'system-created' test. Human touch is audit_log actor_type='human' (inventory script line 58).
- `docs/explanation/home-and-worklist.md:115` — commitmentLocator covers archived tasks, refused proposals and dismissed claims, so withdrawn automatic noise is not recreated.

Reviewed with Claude Code against public source `10d5bdb18`, then reconciled with the existing issue scope and repository rules. The tests above are implementation requirements; this planning review did not run them or implement product changes.

### Included #2674: Today does not yet carry the brief or the digest it claims to unify

#### Implementation plan

Inventory the current attention/brief/digest assembly before adding a producer; several surfaces have evolved since this issue was filed. Reuse the shared ranking and existing brief/receipt lanes to expose material current work once and route routine digest activity to the activity view. Make the OpenAPI and handbook describe exactly which sources the page reads. Keep `as_of` as the per-request RepeatableRead snapshot instant (`assemble.go`, `database.WithWorkspaceSnapshot`), and remove only the claim that `/attention` carries the digest; state that `as_of` does not span `/digest`, `/brief`, `/magic` or a multi-page walk; preserve the bounded walk/freshness and partial-source guarantees from #7975. Do not introduce a cross-module mega-transaction to justify old prose.

#### Acceptance and validation

A material brief item and an overnight receipt are either displayed in their intended section or linked with truthful coverage; they do not duplicate an existing action. Withhold/fail one source and resolve another row mid-read: neither a false complete/zero claim nor an impossible snapshot guarantee appears. Compare API documentation, rendered counts and continuation behavior.

- [ ] The behavior above is implemented through the real owning writers/readers and applicable UI/API/tool surfaces.
- [ ] The owning package's regression tests and required repository checks pass.
- [ ] The PR for #7976 maps this issue to concrete changes and passing tests, and includes `Closes #2674` only when the whole requirement is met.

#### Closure boundary

Resolve this ticket with #7976; do not close it just because a plan was written or the parent was updated. If the behavior is already implemented, verify it and cite the current code/tests before closing. Future Home repair #7977 reuses relevant admission and lifecycle predicates rather than inventing a second fix.

#### Implementation refinements after source review

##### Source findings
- `/attention` claims the digest (`crm.yaml` ~16091, `attention/doc.go:7-10`), but no lane reads it.
- The brief lane's read also writes (it resurfaces snoozes and records the open) through `Detached`, as noted in `worklistsnapshot_integration_test.go:64-76`. That is the one exception to 'one instant'.
- The digest (`morningdigestread.go`) is a stored nightly payload. Its review counts (pending approvals, dedupe candidates) duplicate the live `needs_you` lanes at an older instant.

##### Recommended contract
1. Do not add a digest lane to `Assemble`. Correct the `/attention` description and `doc.go`: the digest is read beside the feed, not inside it.
2. On Home, show the digest's capture totals and connector health in the activity/Magic rail with 'as of the nightly run'. Show live decision counts only from `/worklist`; drop or relabel the digest's approval and dedupe counts so the same queue is never shown with two numbers.
3. Document in `crm.yaml` and the handbook that `as_of` is per endpoint, and that a multi-page walk has no shared database transaction snapshot (its frozen member identities and walk metadata remain meaningful) (already said in `worklist.reads.ts:58`).

##### Tests
- A frontend test: a digest saying 3 pending approvals and a live worklist with 1 → Home shows 1 for decisions and labels the digest figures as nightly.
- `brief.rail.overnight.stories.tsx` covers digest 404/501 next to a populated feed.
- A backend doc gate is optional; `make check`, `make check-fe`, `make fe-uat`.

##### Closure
Close with #7976 when the docs no longer claim digest unification, Home shows no duplicate decision counts, and the partial-source cases (digest missing, lane withheld) render without false zeros.
##### Source checks from the Claude review

- `backend/api/crm.yaml:16091` — 'Five producers ... the overnight digest' and 'One transaction, one instant: as_of stamps the read'.
- `backend/internal/compose/attention/assemble.go:35` — Assemble runs every lane in one inSnapshot; there is no digest lane.
- `backend/internal/platform/database/database.go:222` — WithWorkspaceSnapshot uses pgx.RepeatableRead: a real shared snapshot per request.
- `frontend/src/features/brief/brief.queries.ts:61` — Home reads /digest on its own query; the comment at line 15 says no combined 'my day' payload exists.

Reviewed with Claude Code against public source `10d5bdb18`, then reconciled with the existing issue scope and repository rules. The tests above are implementation requirements; this planning review did not run them or implement product changes.

## Outcome and current code

Home should make current personal decisions, commitments, revenue interventions and meeting preparation easy to understand. It already has one ranking engine and team exception support. Improve those projections after eligibility is corrected; do not create a founder-only scoring engine. Risk amounts in classifyrisk are face values converted to base currency, not expected loss, and routine activity receipts need a different emphasis from material business changes.
## Scope and dependencies

Required prerequisites: #7901, #7968, #7969, #7970, #7953, #7971, #2738, #7972, #7973, #7974, #7975, #2531.

Do not invent a new expected-loss model or redesign the entire CRM. Fix the daily decision experience using the existing attention and design-system owners.

Implementation size: L (relative scope, not a delivery-date promise).

## Code to start from

- `backend/internal/compose/attention/focus.go`
- `backend/internal/compose/attention/ranksteps.go`
- `backend/internal/compose/attention/classifyrisk.go`
- `backend/internal/compose/attention/teamexceptions.go`

- `backend/internal/compose/magic/linerecords.go`
- `frontend/src/features/brief/brief.focus.tsx`
- `frontend/src/features/brief/brief.dials.tsx`
- `frontend/src/features/sign-in/magic.lines.tsx`

## Implementation plan

1. Use the corrected ownership/eligibility facts to select Focus. Keep the current shared ranking and allow fewer cards when few items qualify. Do not hard-code a named user or invent a separate role outside the existing permission model.
2. Present distinct personal decisions, my commitments, waiting-on-others, revenue interventions and meeting preparation within existing components. Team work appears with its owner and the specific help requested.
3. Make cards answer who, what, why me, why now, evidence/state and button effect. An explicit termination/account escalation must be able to outrank routine messages; uncertain data alone must not claim imminent loss.
4. Label the monetary measure as flagged pipeline value unless an actual expected-loss calculation exists. State currency, missing values, scope and the difference between missing CRM fields and evidence of commercial risk.
5. Collapse calendar parsing and routine filing into background activity. Give forecast/stage/owner changes readable before/after, reason, impact and true undo availability; provide a readable fallback for unsupported receipt record kinds.
6. Keep one state and navigation path across Focus, Worklist and needs-you, with the count semantics from #7975. Update handbook, all supported locales and both-theme stories.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A quiet day can show zero or two useful priorities without filler.
- [ ] Every Focus item has a personal responsibility or explicit intervention reason and a concrete action.
- [ ] Historical invitations, newsletters and routine enrichment do not occupy personal Focus.
- [ ] Risk labels match the implemented calculation and show unknown values honestly.
- [ ] Material forecast changes explain their reason; parser metadata does not masquerade as sales progress.
- [ ] No unknown receipt kind silently disappears behind a complete-success claim.

## Validation

Extend attention focus/ranking/team-exception tests, magic receipt tests and brief/magic stories with quiet, busy, uncertain and partial-source days. Include a manager and a rep with different personal responsibilities. Run make check-fe, make fe-uat in both themes, affected integration packages and `make bench-daily` (needs `make db-up`) and `TestTheWorklistFamilyAssemblesInOneTransaction` when assembly/query behavior changes.

## Working agreement

This is one outcome-sized task and normally one PR, including both API and UI where the behavior crosses the wire. Read the named code again before implementing: these paths were checked against main at `10d5bdb18`. Reuse existing owning modules and compose seams; do not add parallel request, commitment, ranking or approval engines.

Use fictional demo data and fixed clocks. First make the stated behavior observable through the real writer/read path; the scenarios below are implementation acceptance fixtures, not a claim that a new failing test was executed while planning. Keep source visibility, workspace boundaries, RBAC, human edits, audit/outbox and replay behavior intact. Contract changes start in backend/api/crm.yaml and regenerate bindings; migrations are additive. Run make check before push and make test-it DIR=<pkg> for every integration package touched. Frontend changes include stories, both themes, supported locales and make fe-uat. Model-rule changes also need the existing AI certification lane; unit tests alone do not establish semantic quality.

No running-install repair, message sending or approval execution is authorized by this implementation issue. #7977 owns the repair mechanism and its preview; operating it is a separately reviewed action.

## Implementation refinements after source review

### Source findings
- One ranking (`ranksteps.go`) and Focus as a cut of it (`focus.go`). `focusLimit` is a cap, not a quota.
- The money is face value in base currency: `expectedRevenue`, `priceDealsAtRiskRow`, `readingsOf`. The UI labels it 'Revenue at risk' (`en.ts` 800, 13612, 13649). The rank step is named `expected_revenue`.
- Home fans out to five endpoints (`brief.queries.ts:15-18`). A Worklist walk is re-ranked on every page (`worklist.reads.ts:58-62`).

### Sequence

Show the currency and the `unpriced_deals` count beside it. Do **not** rename the wire field `expected_minor_base` or the rank step `expected_revenue` (saved snapshots and the contract depend on them); if the internal name misleads, rename only the Go function `expectedRevenue`.
2. **Receipts (no prerequisite):** extend the server projection and `magic.lines.tsx` together: a line discarded by the server cannot be recovered by the client. Provide an authorized generic fallback or truthful coverage state with a 'not described' count, and make the Magic panel's empty or complete state check `not_shown` before saying 'all done'. Move calendar-parse and routine filing lines to the collapsed activity group using the existing `describe.go` vocabulary, not a new classifier.
3. **Forecast changes:** reuse `undojudge.go`/`undoversion.go` for undo availability. Take before/after from `linerecords.go`; put the reason in `reason.key`.
4. **Focus selection (after prerequisites):** keep `focusEligible`. Add only the eligibility facts that #7901/#7968/#7969/#7973 expose, as row fields that `focusEligible` reads, so no second ranker appears. An explicit termination or escalation signal moves up through the existing `levelWaiting`/`levelMaterialRisk` level, not a new score.
5. **Team rows:** use #2531's owner contract (`nameExceptionOwners`); a team row states its owner and the help requested.
6. **#2674:** follow its plan (digest placement and `as_of` wording) in the same PR.

### Edge cases
A mixed-currency day with no FX (`money.converted()` false): the label must not claim base currency. Every deal unpriced: show 'unknown', never 0. A provisional close date stays a forecast prompt. A manager's Focus differs from a rep's on the same deal. A withheld lane shows in `sources_unavailable` and never as a quiet day.

### Tests and commands
- `focus_test.go`: quiet (0 cards), busy (cut at 6 with `urgent_remaining`), termination outranks a routine reply, newsletter/historical/enrichment excluded.
- `readings_test.go`: unpriced and mixed-currency cases. `magic/describe_test.go`: unknown kind, no false complete.
- Stories: `brief.focus.stories.tsx`, `magic.lines.stories.tsx` (quiet, busy, uncertain, partial-source) in both themes.
- `make check-fe`, `make fe-uat`, `make test-it DIR=backend/internal/compose/integration`, `make bench-daily` if assembly changes, then `make check`.

### Closure
The closure table maps each acceptance bullet to a test. Close #7976 and #2674 together only after the listed prerequisites are merged, or are cited as already satisfied. Steps 1–3 may be built earlier on the same branch.
### Source checks from the Claude review

- `backend/internal/compose/attention/classifyrisk.go:151` — expectedRevenue: 'until that read exists the amount stands in for the expectation' — it is face value, not probability-weighted.
- `backend/api/crm.yaml:61490` — expected_minor_base is documented as 'NOT weighted by win_probability'. The contract is already honest; the labels are not.
- `frontend/src/i18n/en.ts:800` — 'brief.readings.risk': 'Revenue at risk'. The same label appears at 13612 (worklist.exceptions.kind.revenue_at_risk) and 13649 (worklist.readings.revenue).
- `backend/internal/compose/attention/focus.go:51` — focusEligible already has per-source rules and focusLimit=6 is a maximum, so a quiet day already allows fewer cards.
- `backend/internal/compose/magic/done.go:157` — notShownSince reports unknown_entity_type only to seats with ai_diagnostics read; for others the absence is not a zero.
- `backend/internal/compose/attention/readings.go:46` — readingsOf leaves unpriced deals out and counts them (UnpricedDeals), and dedupes by deal id.

Reviewed with Claude Code against public source `10d5bdb18`, then reconciled with the existing issue scope and repository rules. The tests above are implementation requirements; this planning review did not run them or implement product changes.

### Included #5343: Assurance rule: a buying-intent signal with no deal to attach it to

#### Implementation plan

Add a signal-subject assurance scan and its subject authorization/list/resolve path, because the current Rule/Subject and resolver are deal-only. Reuse the existing exception storage and writer; a coverage count alone does not implement the required finding. Reuse the Deal Scout eligibility and buyer-attribution decision via a compose seam. Use the existing source/signal identity to refer to one commercial matter: if an active deal suggestion already covers the signal, the finding links to that suggestion instead of creating a second actionable card. If a suitable deal is later linked/created, resolve or supersede the unlinked finding and suggestion through their owning writers. Do not reopen dismissed evidence without material new information.

#### Acceptance and validation

A current buyer signal without a deal yields one reachable review matter. Adding a matching deal resolves the orphan state; a rejected suggestion is not resurrected by assurance. Partner copies, suppliers, duplicates and old detected-now evidence fail the same eligibility rules as Deal Scout. Verify event replay and multiple genuine opportunities at one company remain distinct.

- [ ] The behavior above is implemented through the real owning writers/readers and applicable UI/API/tool surfaces.
- [ ] The owning package's regression tests and required repository checks pass.

Future Home repair #7977 reuses relevant admission and lifecycle predicates rather than inventing a second fix.

#### Implementation refinements after source review

##### Implement an actual unlinked-signal finding

The existing assurance Rule/Subject model and resolve authorization are deal-only, although storage anticipates signal subjects. This is a real missing implementation seam. Reporting only eligible_signals would not fulfill this ticket's request for a finding.

1. Add a narrowly scoped signal-subject scan path within assurance, supplied through compose by the existing signals/Deal Scout eligibility owners. Keep current deal rules unchanged. The input carries verified signal/company/source references and eligibility facts, not copied private message text. Use the same buyer/time rules as #7974 rather than cloning its SQL/model decisions.
2. Extend subject-specific authorization, list/detail/resolve behavior and generated contracts for signal findings through the owning modules. A caller who cannot read the underlying subject must not receive its existence, label or evidence via a finding. Reuse the exception writer's audit/outbox and stable logical identity.
3. Represent the commercial matter once in attention: when a valid Deal Scout suggestion covers the signal, the assurance finding links to that suggestion and the shared projection groups the action. If no suggestion can be made, retain a meaningful qualification/link-existing review route. A count is coverage metadata, not that route.
4. On link/create/dismiss or new material evidence, update the finding and suggestion through their respective module writers. Preserve rejection floors, replay identity and distinct signals; do not reopen dismissed evidence or declare unrelated company signals resolved.

Tests use the real assurance scan/resolver plus Deal Scout: current unlinked buying intent creates a finding; a covered suggestion yields one actionable matter; link/create resolves the applicable orphan state; dismissal/replay cannot resurrect it; a supplier or old detected-now signal is excluded; hidden evidence stays hidden. ### Included #7908: Mark captured history as settled during the first import

#### Implementation plan

Add an optional mailbox-history baseline as a per-connection setting beside `PUT /connectors/{provider}/mail-posture` (shown on `CaptureConnection` and offered in the backfill dialog), not in the workspace-wide `/capture/settings`. The UI means “do not suggest automatic obligations from before this date,” not “everything was fulfilled.” Persist the scope, selected date, timezone and actor through the owning module with audit/outbox. ## Outcome and current code

Deal Scout admits a held meeting, proposal-like outbound attachment, or a paired opportunity/commitment signal. Signals are timed by detected_at; attachments without company_id use the activity company reach set. These are candidate-discovery rules, not proof of current buyer identity or a distinct opportunity. Confidence currently combines evidence kinds, not the number of duplicate attachments; preserve that distinction.

Demo scenario: a transcript provider carries a client meeting; a proposal is copied to a partner; a company has a networking meeting, a supplier offer and a genuine scoped buyer request. An old request is extracted today.
## Scope and dependencies

Required prerequisites: #7901, #7973.

Implementation size: L (relative scope, not a delivery-date promise).

## Code to start from

- `backend/internal/compose/dealscoutsql.go`
- `backend/internal/compose/dealscoutdraft.go`
- `backend/internal/compose/dealscoutdocument.go`
- `backend/internal/compose/dealscout_integration_test.go`
- `backend/internal/compose/dealscoutreview_integration_test.go`
- `frontend/src/features/worklist/worklist.suggestion.tsx`

## Implementation plan

1. Resolve the actual buying company and commercial direction from source participants and supported document/signal context. Keep provider, partner, supplier and end-customer roles separate; ambiguous attribution stays a qualification item.
2. Use source occurrence time for freshness and distinguish it from signal detected_at. Recheck current existing deals/projects, dismissed suggestions and later outcome before creating a new suggestion.
3. Deduplicate evidence by stable source/document identity, keeping legitimate revisions distinct. Do not claim confidence rises with duplicate attachment count; make displayed corroboration represent independent kinds/sources.
4. Split candidate qualification from proposing a new deal. Offer qualify, link-existing and not-a-deal with explicit reasons by extending the existing `/deal-suggestions/{id}/accept` and `/dismiss` contract (today: no dismiss reason, no link-existing verb) rather than a second opportunity pipeline.
5. Show owner, current need, next step, source age and company-attribution uncertainty. Keep high-value current leads visible while routing simple meeting follow-up to the attending seller.
6. Coordinate with #5343 so a buying signal with no deal is not two independent obligations in assurance and Deal Scout.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A provider or copied partner is not automatically treated as the buyer of the attached proposal.
- [ ] A meeting alone, supplier offer or event invitation is a qualification/relationship item, not a confident new sales opportunity.
- [ ] Old evidence extracted today does not acquire a fresh commercial date.
- [ ] One existing opportunity is linked rather than duplicated. At a company with an open deal, a distinct current expansion is surfaced for explicit human qualification (link, or create by hand), because `deals.SuggestionCompanyFreeClause` blocks any automatic suggestion there; relaxing that shared clause needs a `status: needs-decision` product decision.
- [ ] Repeated copies do not inflate displayed evidence or confidence, and uncertainty remains reviewable.

## Validation

Extend Deal Scout SQL/real-writer integration tests with provider/partner participants, repeated document identity, revisions, old signal occurrence/new detection, existing closed/open opportunities and a current valid buyer request. Test the frontend qualification actions against the contract. Integrations: compose and modules/deals.

## Working agreement

This is one outcome-sized task and normally one PR, including both API and UI where the behavior crosses the wire. Read the named code again before implementing: these paths were checked against main at `10d5bdb18`. Reuse existing owning modules and compose seams; do not add parallel request, commitment, ranking or approval engines.

Use fictional demo data and fixed clocks. First make the stated behavior observable through the real writer/read path; the scenarios below are implementation acceptance fixtures, not a claim that a new failing test was executed while planning. Keep source visibility, workspace boundaries, RBAC, human edits, audit/outbox and replay behavior intact. Contract changes start in backend/api/crm.yaml and regenerate bindings; migrations are additive. Run make check before push and make test-it DIR=<pkg> for every integration package touched. Frontend changes include stories, both themes, supported locales and make fe-uat. Model-rule changes also need the existing AI certification lane; unit tests alone do not establish semantic quality.

No running-install repair, message sending or approval execution is authorized by this implementation issue. #7977 owns the repair mechanism and its preview; operating it is a separately reviewed action.

## Implementation refinements after source review

### Preserve evidence time, buyer identity and recovery

Deal Scout already shares suggestion floors, an open-deal constraint and stale-suggestion retirement across its read/write/accept paths. Preserve those guards while fixing admission and review.

1. Resolve each evidence item's actual cited source occurrence time through the existing evidence parser and activities reader. Detection time is processing metadata, not a freshness fallback. Missing source time stays unknown and prevents a confident automatic proposal; do not make an old event fresh by extracting it today. Keep source-time comparisons consistent in candidate selection, writer rechecks and acceptance/dismissal floors. A fresh new buyer message must remain distinguishable from an old attachment in the same evidence set.
2. Identify the actual buyer using verified participants, commercial role and source/document context. Neither every reachable company nor only To-recipients is a valid buyer rule: a real buyer can be CC'd and a partner can be in To. Ambiguity becomes an explicit qualification item, not a guessed company. Reuse #2690's corrected domain identity.
3. Deduplicate actual content/source identity after verifying the available attachment fields; preserve revisions and distinct opportunities. Keep confidence's existing distinct-kind semantics. A meeting or supplier pitch alone is not a low-confidence new-deal proposal disguised as qualification.
4. Extend the existing suggestion contract for reasoned dismissal and link-existing, with scoped target checks, module-owned audit/outbox, replay behavior and UI/tool parity. Current code has accept/dismiss only; do not describe new verbs as already implemented.
5. Preserve the current one-open-suggestion/open-deal guard. A distinct expansion at an account with an open deal can be surfaced for human qualification/link/manual creation; changing the automatic guard is not necessary for this package. Verify every shared reader/writer/accept path rather than relaxing one copy.
6. Include the full #5343 signal-finding path and the historical recovery obligation from #7908. After the #7908 baseline added in this package is set, a genuinely relevant old quiet opportunity remains discoverable as explicitly historical recovery when evidence supports it. It must not masquerade as a fresh buyer signal or overdue personal commitment. This completes #7908 only after its earlier baseline tests and this recovery case pass.

Test current buyer intent, partner/provider/supplier messages, buyer-on-CC, multiple candidate companies, missing/old source time, detected-now history, duplicate/revised files, link-existing, dismissal replay, existing open deals and the baseline/recovery pair. Run real compose/deals/assurance integrations, frontend UAT and `make check`. Close #7974, #5343 and #7908 only with their complete respective evidence.

- `backend/internal/compose/dealscoutsql.go:43` — Signals enter evidence with s.detected_at as occurred_at, so an old ask extracted today looks fresh.
- `backend/internal/compose/dealscoutsql.go:56` — Attachments with no company_id are filed to every company in CompanyReachSet; a partner on cc becomes a candidate buyer.
- `backend/internal/compose/dealscoutsql.go:73` — The chosen CTE groups by company_id, so there is one suggestion per company and no per-opportunity identity.
- `backend/internal/compose/dealscoutdraft.go:58` — scoutConfidence weighs distinct kinds only; duplicate copies already do not raise confidence, though cited evidence can still list copies up to dealScoutItemCap.
- `backend/internal/modules/deals/suggestion.go:142` — SuggestionCompanyFreeClause blocks any suggestion while the company has an open deal; scout, writer, superseding pass and accept all compose it.
- `backend/internal/modules/deals/suggestion.go:312` — SupersedeStaleSuggestionsTx already retires open suggestions when the company gains an open deal.
- `backend/api/crm.yaml:5223` — dismissDealSuggestion takes no reason; no link-existing operation exists under /deal-suggestions.

## Outcome and current code

readContradictions selects an open contract_ended signal per company and offerStageChange stages a company lifecycle move from its summary. It does not pass source evidence into StageInput. The accept effect compares lifecycle and acknowledges every open contract_ended signal for the company. A workstream ending is not necessarily the end of the company relationship.

Demo scenario: Cedar Labs has an active support engagement and a separate declined pilot. A newer signed build agreement arrives while a former-customer proposal waits.
## Scope and dependencies

Required prerequisites: #7971.

Implementation size: L (relative scope, not a delivery-date promise).

## Code to start from

- `backend/internal/compose/signalproposals.go`
- `backend/internal/compose/signalproposals_integration_test.go`
- `backend/internal/modules/contacts/companylifecycle.go`
- `backend/internal/modules/approvals/redeem.go`
- `backend/internal/compose/company360/suggestions.go` (`lifecycleConflict`, `liveLifecycles`) and `company360/signalfacts.go` (newest open contract_ended read)
- `backend/internal/modules/signals/derived.go` (`AcknowledgeOpenForCompanyTx`)
- `backend/internal/modules/approvals/autonomy.go` (`lifecycle_change` is auto-apply eligible)

## Implementation plan

1. Trace each lifecycle signal to its readable source occurrence time, evidence and affected contract/deal/workstream. Treat unknown scope as unresolved, not whole-company termination.
2. Add a compose-owned reconciliation seam over existing module readers for current engagements and newer contradictory evidence. Share the judgment with company360 lifecycle-conflict presentation; do not leave the two readers with conflicting rules.
3. Stage a proposal only with a clear company-level consequence, or show a review-needed conflict without recommending the move. Attach the actual source evidence and name which workstream ended.
4. Recheck evidence/scope/current engagement state inside the supported decision/effect boundary, using existing lock/version patterns. New conflicting evidence makes a proposal stale or in need of review; it must not silently apply.
5. Acknowledge only the signals the decision actually resolves. Preserve separate workstream facts and later/new signals. Present related won/owner/lifecycle proposals together for context without implying one approval authorizes all of them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Declining one pilot does not alone recommend ending an account with another active engagement.
- [ ] A true account-wide termination with adequate evidence remains actionable.
- [ ] New evidence arriving after staging is checked again before application, including concurrent changes.
- [ ] The preview names source/date/scope and any unresolved conflict; no claim is based only on extraction time.
- [ ] Resolving one change does not acknowledge unrelated contract-ended signals.

## Validation

Extend signalproposals_integration_test.go and company360 lifecycle tests with two engagements, contradictory source dates, stale proposals, simultaneous writes and a valid company-wide termination. Test both human and automatic-change release paths through their real effects. Integrations: compose, compose/integration, modules/contacts and modules/approvals.

## Working agreement

This is one outcome-sized task and normally one PR, including both API and UI where the behavior crosses the wire. Read the named code again before implementing: these paths were checked against main at `10d5bdb18`. Reuse existing owning modules and compose seams; do not add parallel request, commitment, ranking or approval engines.

Use fictional demo data and fixed clocks. First make the stated behavior observable through the real writer/read path; the scenarios below are implementation acceptance fixtures, not a claim that a new failing test was executed while planning. Keep source visibility, workspace boundaries, RBAC, human edits, audit/outbox and replay behavior intact. Contract changes start in backend/api/crm.yaml and regenerate bindings; migrations are additive. Run make check before push and make test-it DIR=<pkg> for every integration package touched. Frontend changes include stories, both themes, supported locales and make fe-uat. Model-rule changes also need the existing AI certification lane; unit tests alone do not establish semantic quality.

No running-install repair, message sending or approval execution is authorized by this implementation issue. #7977 owns the repair mechanism and its preview; operating it is a separately reviewed action.

## Implementation refinements after source review

### One lifecycle reconciliation, checked before writing

Source confirms two rule copies (`readContradictions` and company360.lifecycleConflict), missing staging evidence, company-wide signal acknowledgement and an auto-apply path. The reconciliation must govern that automatic path as well as a human's preview.

1. Build one compose predicate over module-owned reads of signal provenance/source time, workstream scope, current engagements and contradictory evidence. Use bounded, explicit evidence; recent mail or an open CRM deal alone is not proof of either continued or ended company-wide business. Return company-wide, scoped/unknown or contradicted with reasons. Both card and proposer consume it; remove the deliberate duplicate-rule comment.
2. Stage a company-wide lifecycle change only with affirmative company-wide evidence. Missing workstream scope defaults to an unresolved/reviewable signal, not inferred termination. Attach supported typed evidence references and record the exact covered signal IDs and relevant versions. Existing scope-less signals must not silently disappear from review.
3. Inside the existing redemption transaction, acquire/revalidate the target and relevant evidence versions BEFORE `SetCompanyLifecycleTx`. Then invoke the normal writer. Do not mutate the lifecycle first and reconcile against the already-changed state. Define the lock/version protocol that detects concurrent contradictory evidence, including evidence arriving during the decision, and exercise it in both human and auto-apply tests.
4. Acknowledge only the verified covered signals through a signals-owned ID-scoped writer. Later/unrelated signals remain open. Decode legacy payloads conservatively and revalidate their single referenced signal; never fall back to acknowledging every open company signal.
5. Related deal/owner approvals remain separate decisions. Preserve durable rejection identity and pass the same versioned predicate to #7977.

Test a terminated pilot with ongoing support, positive whole-company termination evidence, missing scope, newer agreement evidence, concurrent decisions/evidence writes, legacy proposals, partial acknowledgement and replay. Prove the card, proposer and both execution paths agree. Run touched compose/signals/contacts/approvals integrations and `make check`; close only when preview and actual writes obey the same rule.
### Source checks from the Claude review

- `backend/internal/compose/signalproposals.go:169` — `readContradictions`: DISTINCT ON company, ordered by `s.detected_at DESC`. It has no source occurrence time, no scope, and no check of other live engagements.
- `backend/internal/compose/signalproposals.go:217` — `StageUnlessDeclined` input has no `Evidence`, although `approvals.StageInput` supports it (commitmentdispatch.go:288 uses it).
- `backend/internal/compose/signalproposals.go:279` — The accept effect calls `signals.AcknowledgeOpenForCompanyTx(..., signalKindContractEnded)` and settles all signals for the company.
- `backend/internal/compose/company360/suggestions.go:360` — `lifecycleConflict` is the card-side rule (`liveLifecycles`, line 398). Its Reason/Title are English literals, which the #2493 census also covers.
- `backend/internal/modules/contacts/companylifecycle.go:58` — `SetCompanyLifecycleTx` locks the company row FOR UPDATE and compares `from`. This is the existing concurrency guard for the stage itself, but not for the evidence.
- `backend/internal/modules/approvals/autonomy.go:135` — `lifecycle_change` is eligible for automatic apply, so the effect runs with no human preview.

Reviewed with Claude Code against public source `10d5bdb18`, then reconciled with the existing issue scope and repository rules. The tests above are implementation requirements; this planning review did not run them or implement product changes.

title: Without a system mail relay, a confirmation request mints a link that can never reach the contact

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: priority: normal
labels.description: Real but narrow, guarded or latent; hygiene, test-lane work, polish

labels.name: area: privacy
labels.description: Erasure, retention, consent

labels.name: status: in progress
labels.description: Somebody is working on this - see the assignee. Do not pick it up

body:
## What happens

On an installation without a system mail relay, "Request confirmation of details" on a contact mints the link and then says: "The link was created for {address} but not sent, because this installation sends no email." The user's own mailbox sends fine, so the sentence reads as false, and it offers nothing to do next. The link cannot be passed on by hand either: the server deliberately never returns the token.

Decided behaviour: an installation needs a system mail relay to send confirmation requests. When it has none, the product says so plainly and points to the fix, instead of minting a link nobody can use.

## How to reproduce

1. `make dev` with an instance config that has no `email:` block (the default).
2. Open any contact with an email address, go to the consent section and choose "Request confirmation of details".
3. The notice above appears; the response carries `queued: false` and `sendable: false`.

## Where it comes from

- Frontend: `frontend/src/features/privacy/consent.tsx:399-401` picks `consent.askQueued` or `consent.askNotDelivered` from `queued` alone and ignores `sendable`.
- Backend: `POST /contacts/{id}/consent/confirm-request` (`backend/internal/modules/consent/confirmmail.go`) mints the token even when no lane is wired; `stageConfirmMail` (`confirmstage.go`) returns a zero delivery, and `canSendConfirm()` reports `sendable=false`.
- The lane needs the operator relay, which only `WithOperatorMail` sets, and only when the instance config's `email.enabled` is true (`backend/cmd/api/main.go`, `passwordResetOptions`; `backend/internal/compose/controllermailwiring.go`, `rewireConfirmationLane`).
- The API description of `ConfirmRequestIssued` (`backend/api/crm.yaml`) says `sendable=false` means the link "must be passed on by hand", which the product does not allow.

## Suggested fix and acceptance

- When `sendable` is false, the consent section does not offer "Request confirmation of details" as a working action. It says that system mail is not set up, that an admin sets it up, and links to the configuration reference for the `email:` block.
- The endpoint refuses to mint a token it cannot deliver (no unusable link, no 201 for a request that cannot complete), with an error that names the missing relay.
- The `ConfirmRequestIssued` description matches what the product does.
- Other controller mail on the same lane (privacy notices, double opt-in) is checked for the same dead end and treated the same way.
- Tests: with no relay, the action is not offered and the endpoint refuses; with a relay, behaviour is unchanged.

## Context

Module: consent (`backend/internal/modules/consent`), frontend privacy. Commit: 9aba59033. Reported by a user.
